100	- **The health tracker is generic** (`sensor_health`), not light-only, so the soil process can reuse it. It is a small public struct with no malloc.
101	- **Health input:** any non-`GT_OK` result from `gt_light_read` counts as one failure. The driver's 3 retries are already inside a single failed read.
102	- **Health output:** `gt_health_record` returns a transition event (`NONE` / `OFFLINE` / `ONLINE`) and the caller logs it. The tracker does no I/O.
103	- **Time is passed in** as `now_ms`, matching `gt_sampler_tick`, so tests need no clock.
104	- **Test ID prefixes:** `SHR` (sensor health record), `SHS` (sensor health should-read), `SHE` (sensor health event name), `LGF` (log format), `MSE` (message encode), `MSD` (message decode), `CRC` (CRC-32), `RCE` (record encode), `RCD` (record decode), `IFD` (IPC frame decode), `ICO` (IPC client open), `ICC` (IPC client close), `ICS` (IPC client send), `ICR` (IPC client reconnect), `IOV` (IPC client overflow), `IPL` (IPC loopback over a real socket).
105	- **Log ownership:** the light sensor's events (`i2c_read_error`, `sensor_offline`, `sensor_online`) are Lily's, as the light process's read-failure handling. The shared formatter (`gt_log_format`) has no owner in the Ownership map because every component uses it, so it counts as **Joint → Architecture integration**. Lily writes it first, as its first caller; give Lucas a heads-up so his components reuse it.
106	- **Log line:** `<timestamp_us> <LEVEL> <component> <event>[ key=value ...]`. The timestamp is µs since the Unix epoch, as a plain integer, the same unit as the on-disk record, so logs and records can be joined. The levels are `DEBUG` / `INFO` / `WARN` / `ERROR`. The light process logs `sensor_offline` as WARN and `sensor_online` as INFO.
107	- **Log sink: stderr** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-18). The formatter only fills a caller-provided buffer, and every process writes the finished `gt_log_format` line to stderr, as `storage_main` already does. Children inherit the supervisor's stderr, so under systemd every line lands in the journal. Each process still reads the wall clock for its own timestamps. A shared file sink was rejected (rotation becomes our problem), and so was sending lines to the monitor process (it waits on Mechanism E).
108	- **Hop 2 (hub→storage) carries the 24 B on-disk record** (decided 2026-10-23). The hub stamps `seq` and the µs timestamp, builds the record (CRC included), and storage checks it (amended 2026-10-26, PF-01: the timestamp is stamped on arrival, `seq` + CRC at send time; see *Hub contract (hop 2)*) with `gt_record_decode`, then appends it unchanged. There are two reasons. First, DESIGN.md already has the hub stamping the time and storage reading *records* from `storage.sock`. Second, a record that waits in the hub's 1024-record queue during a storage outage (up to about 17 min) keeps its real receive time. If storage stamped the time instead, the timestamp would be off by however long the record waited.
109	- **The hub's next `seq` after connecting to storage is max(own next, `seq_resume` + 1)** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-03). A freshly started hub has no counter, so it takes storage's reply + 1 (0 on an empty log). A running hub keeps its own counter, defined as 1 + the last `seq` whose `send()` succeeded, so records storage lost in a `kill -9` (unsynced, or still in the socket) leave a hole that storage turns into a GAP (`recovery_gap`). The alternative, always continuing from the reply, was rejected: it reuses the lost `seq`s, so the loss leaves no GAP and the hub's sent log holds duplicates, which breaks "no reading is lost silently" and the Evaluation plan's lost-readings formula. Only a loss where the hub restarts too (power cut) is shown by `unclean_shutdown` alone, which DESIGN.md's Power row already allows. Storage needed no change: its sequence guard already writes the GAP. This rule sets what PF-01 (when to stamp) and PF-02 (the sender's states) must support, and what `storage_faults.sh` checks (PF-04/05).
110	- **Hub contract for hop 2** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-01/PF-02): the hub stamps the time on arrival and `seq` + CRC at send; the socket seam gains `recv`; the sender waits for `seq_resume` (2 s deadline) before sending anything. See *Hub contract (hop 2)*.
111	- **Message magic is `0xA6`** (proposed), distinct from the on-disk record's `0xA7`, so a record can never be misread as a message.
112	- **Truncated messages are rejected at `recv()`,** which must return exactly `GT_MSG_SIZE`, not in decode. Decode keeps its fixed 16 B array.
113	- **Range checks stay in the hub:** decode doesn't check that light ≤ 65535. That is the hub's `reading_invalid` check.
114	- **Deferred:** `src/light_sensor_main.c` (open → sample → health → send) waited until the IPC client existed. The client was completed on 2026-10-24, so it is now the next item (see *Not done yet*).
115	- **`hub.sock` is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`** (decided 2026-10-24). The kernel keeps message boundaries, so each `send()` is one whole 16 B message and each `recv()` returns exactly one message. A short message shows up as a short `recv()`, which is where DESIGN.md rejects it, and there are no partial sends to track. `SOCK_STREAM` would need frame reassembly and resync code in the hub.
116	- **`hub_listen` stands in for the hub on the Pi** (decided 2026-10-24) until `gt_hub_accept` and the hub process exist. It's a small tool (`src/hub_listen_main.c`, `make hub_listen`) that prints each decoded message and flags counter gaps. With it, the kill -9 / kill -STOP fault tests can run now.
117	- **The client never blocks the sampler:** every socket call is non-blocking, and `send` uses `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, so a dead hub returns `EPIPE` instead of raising SIGPIPE, which would kill the sensor process.
118	- **Time is passed in** (`now_ms` on `gt_ipc_client_send` / `_pump`), as with the health tracker, so the backoff tests need no clock and no sleeps.
119	- **Events are returned, not logged:** the client returns `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` / `_RECONNECT` / `_OVERFLOW` bit flags, and the caller logs `ipc_disconnect` / `ipc_reconnect` / `ipc_overflow`, the same pattern as `gt_health_record`.
120	- **`gt_ipc_client_open` doesn't connect.** A hub that isn't up yet is not an error (DESIGN.md, Mechanism E: processes tolerate unavailable peers at startup). The first attempt happens on the first send or pump.
121	- **GAP needs 2 free slots:** after an overflow, a new reading is accepted only when the ring can hold both the GAP and the reading. This keeps the order: old data, then the GAP, then new data. Otherwise the reading is refused and counted into the same gap.
122	- **Close drops the buffer:** `gt_ipc_client_close` sends nothing more. Readings still in the ring are lost, and that's documented, not silent.
123	- **Limitation (no app-level ack):** a message the kernel accepted but the hub never `recv()`d before dying is lost. The hub sees the jump in the counter as a `sensor_seq_gap`.
124	- **`gt_ipc_client_open_ops` is declared in `ipc_sock.h`, not `ipc.h`** (Step 11). `ipc_sock.h` includes `ipc.h`, so putting it in `ipc.h` would make the two headers include each other. `gt_light_open_bus` sits next to its seam in `light_sensor.h` for the same reason.
125	- **Ownership of the ctx:** once `ops` is non-NULL, the client owns the ctx and calls `destroy` exactly once, from `close` or straight away if the client can't be allocated. With NULL ops there's no `destroy` to call, so the caller keeps the ctx.
126	- **`send` drains, pushes, then drains again** (Step 18). Draining before the push sends older frames first, which can free the slot the new reading needs, so a reading isn't refused when the hub could already have taken the backlog.
127	- **Any send result other than OK or FULL counts as the hub gone** (Step 19): disconnect, report `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` and retry after the wait. Both failure paths (a failed connect and a lost hub) share `schedule_retry`, so the wait doubles the same way for each.
128	- **Order moved to fit the link** (decided 2026-10-24). Every test binary links every file in `src/`, so nothing in `src/` may call a function that doesn't exist yet. `gt_ipc_client_open` calls `gt_ipc_sock_linux`, so it moved from Step 16 to Step 22, and its tests ICO-03/04 moved from Step 15 to Step 21. ICC-03 needs `send` to leave a frame in the ring, so it moved from Step 17 to Step 18.
129	- **One listener per socket, enforced by a lock** (decided 2026-10-24). A process that listens on a socket (`hub_listen` now; the hub and storage later) first takes an `fcntl` write lock on `<socket>.lock` and holds it for its whole life. Only the lock holder may remove a leftover socket file and bind a new one; a second copy prints `already running` and exits without touching anything. The kernel drops the lock when the holder dies, `kill -9` included, so a crash never leaves a stale lock. This is safer than probing with `connect()`, which leaves a gap: two copies started together could both see the file as stale, and the second would take the first one's address. Closing *any* fd the process holds on the lock file releases the lock, so the file is opened in one place only. When the hub is written, this moves into a shared `src/` helper; testing it needs `fork()`, because a process never blocks on its own `fcntl` lock.
130	- **Hub range check for soil rejects only `0xFFFF`** (decided 2026-10-27). That is the seesaw's error code; every other raw count is stored, so an open-air or very wet reading is kept and flagged rather than dropped. It sits behind `GT_HUB_SOIL_RAW_MAX` (`0xFFFE`), which Lucas can tighten once the soil driver exists. Light stays 0–65535. The nominal 200–2000 range was rejected: readings just outside it would be lost.
131	- **A sensor restart is logged, not turned into a GAP** (decided 2026-10-27). When a sensor's new connection starts with a counter below the one expected (the process restarted and its counter went back to 0), the hub logs `sensor_restart last_seen_us=… first_us=…` and writes no GAP record. The hub can't know how many readings the dead process lost, so any count would be made up; the two timestamps show the hole. A GAP with count 0 and one with a count estimated from the elapsed time were both rejected.
132	- **The hub is built before `light_sensor_main.c`** (decided 2026-10-27). The hub steps are H1–H9 and the light process is H10 (*Hub steps*), so the last step runs sensor → hub → storage end to end.
133	- **The socket seam is for clients; servers call the socket API directly** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-16). Clients (`gt_ipc_client`, and later the hub's hop-2 sender) go through `gt_sock_ops`, because their backoff, ring and resume logic is worth testing against a fake with no real waiting. Servers (`listen_sock.c`, `storage_server.c`, and later the hub's rx loop) call `socket` / `bind` / `listen` / `accept` / `recv` / `send` themselves and are tested over real sockets in a `/tmp` directory (LBD, SSV, and later the hub loopback). A server loop is mostly "wait in `poll()`, then hand the bytes on", which a real socket tests well. A server-side seam with its own fake was rejected: it would add an ops table and a second fake to test very little logic.
134	
135	## Wire format: sensor → hub message (16 B, little-endian, encoded byte by byte)
136	| Off | Size | Field | Value |
137	|---|---|---|---|
138	| 0 | 1 | magic | `GT_MSG_MAGIC` = `0xA6` |
139	| 1 | 1 | version | `GT_MSG_VERSION` = 1 |
140	| 2 | 1 | type | `GT_MSG_DATA` = 1, `GT_MSG_GAP` = 2 (same values as `gt_rec_type`) |
141	| 3 | 1 | sensor_id | 1 light, 2 soil (0 = all is not valid on hop 1) |
142	| 4 | 4 | counter | sensor-side counter (for a GAP: the first refused counter) |
143	| 8 | 4 | seq | 0 from the sensor; the hub stamps it |
144	| 12 | 4 | value | DATA: raw count; GAP: refused-reading count |
145	
146	Magic and version are written by encode and checked by decode. They are not `gt_msg` fields; `type` becomes one.
147	
148	## Wire format: hub → storage record (24 B)
149	Hop 2 sends the on-disk record exactly as DESIGN.md *In what format → Record* lays it out: magic `0xA7`, type, version, sensor_id, seq (u32 at 4), timestamp (u64 µs at 8), value (u32 at 16) and CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 (at 20). `gt_record` and the codec live in `include/log_record.h`. **Watch the header order:** the record goes magic, **type, version**, sensor_id, while the message goes magic, **version, type**, sensor_id. Don't copy the message encoder without swapping those two bytes. Unlike the message, a GAP record may use sensor_id 0 (all).
150	
151	## Hub contract (hop 2): stamping, numbering and the sender
152	Decided 2026-10-26 to settle PF-01 and PF-02 (Pipeline-Findings.md) before any hub code exists. It builds on the PF-03 numbering rule in *Decisions*. **Built 2026-10-28** in hub steps H1–H7, test first (see *Hub steps*).
153	
154	**Why it changes (PF-01):** a hub that has just started doesn't know its next `seq` until storage's `seq_resume` reply arrives. Storage may be down or still recovering, and Mechanism E says the hub must keep running anyway. So the hub can't finish a record (`seq` + CRC) when the sensor message arrives. It finishes it when it sends it.
155	
156	### Who stamps what, and when
157	| Field | Set by | When | Why |
158	|---|---|---|---|
159	| `type`, `sensor_id`, `value` | `gt_hub_accept` | message arrives | copied from the checked message |
160	| `timestamp_us` | `gt_hub_accept` (`now_us` passed in) | message arrives | keeps the real receive time while the record waits in the queue (the 2026-10-23 reason still holds) |
161	| `seq` | the hop-2 sender | just before `send()` | only the sender knows the next `seq` (max rule) |
162	| CRC-32 | `gt_record_encode`, called by the sender | just before `send()` | the CRC covers `seq`, so it can't be computed earlier |
163	
164	- **`gt_hub_accept`'s new contract:** validate, range-check and de-duplicate one `gt_msg`. On `GT_OK`, fill `*out` with type, sensor, value and `timestamp_us = now_us`, and leave `seq` at 0. The hub plan adds the event flags it returns (`reading_invalid`, `ipc_duplicate`, `sensor_seq_gap`). They're outside this contract.
165	- **The queue holds unstamped `gt_record`s:** 1024 slots of the in-memory struct (24 B with padding), so DESIGN.md's "1024 records × 24 B" budget still holds. A queued record has no `seq` and no CRC yet.
166	- **A `seq` is used only when `send()` returns `GT_OK`.** The sender stamps the queue head with `next_seq` and encodes it. On OK it drops the record and adds 1 to `next_seq`. On FULL or IO the record stays at the head, unchanged, and `next_seq` doesn't move, so a failed send never makes a hole in the numbering.
167	
168	### The max rule, shared
169	- **`gt_next_seq`** (pure, in `include/storage_proto.h` next to `gt_resume`, because it says what the reply means): `gt_status gt_next_seq(int has_own, uint32_t own_next, const gt_resume *resume, uint32_t *next_out)`. It sets `*next_out` to max(`own_next`, `resume->seq` + 1). With `has_own` 0 (a fresh sender) it uses `resume->seq` + 1, or 0 when `resume->has_last` is 0. `GT_ERR_INVAL` for NULL arguments; `GT_ERR_FULL` when the reply's `seq` is `UINT32_MAX` (no next `seq` exists); `*next_out` is untouched on failure. Built and tested 2026-10-26 (NSQ 8/8).
170	- **Both callers use it:** the hop-2 sender and `storage_feed` (PF-04/05; `storage_feed` done 2026-10-26). The fault rounds then test the same numbering code the hub runs. `storage_proto.c` is Mechanism D's file, so give Lucas a heads-up.
171	
172	### The socket seam gains `recv` (PF-02)
173	`gt_sock_ops` adds one op. The sensor client never calls it, but `src/ipc_sock.c` and `tests/fake_sock.h` both implement it:
174	```c
175	/* Receive one whole message into buf (cap bytes). Non-blocking.
176	 * GT_OK with *len_out = the message length, or *len_out = 0 when nothing
177	 * is waiting (EAGAIN); GT_ERR_IO when the peer closed (recv returns 0) or
178	 * reset the connection. */
179	gt_status (*recv)(void *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t cap, size_t *len_out);
180	```
181	- **The sender reads into `GT_RESUME_SIZE + 1` bytes**, like the storage and hub receivers, so an oversized reply shows up as too long.
182	- **`tests/fake_sock.h` grows:** scripted `recv` replies (bytes, "nothing yet", or IO), and its `sent` frames sized to 24 B as well as 16 B (they are fixed at `GT_MSG_SIZE` today).
183	- `gt_ipc_sock_linux(path)` already takes any path and sends any length, so it serves `storage.sock` unchanged apart from `recv`.
184	
185	### Sender state machine (`include/hub_sender.h`, `src/hub_sender.c`)
186	```
187	              connect() OK → resume_deadline = now + 2000 ms
188	 DISCONNECTED ─────────────────────────────────────────────▶ AWAITING_RESUME
189	   ▲  attempt only when now ≥ next_attempt                        │ recv nothing yet → stay (until the deadline)
190	   │  backoff 100 ms → 2 s, as the client                         │ valid 8 B reply → gt_next_seq → SENDING
191	   │◀── deadline passes, or a bad / wrong-size reply ─────────────┤
192	   │    (ipc_bad_message), or recv IO: disconnect, retry later    │
193	   │                                                              ▼
194	   └──── send IO (EPIPE / ECONNRESET): head record kept ───── SENDING: drain oldest first,
195	         unstamped, storage_unreachable once                    stamp seq + encode + send;
196	                                                                FULL → stop, stay connected
197	```
198	- **Nothing is sent before the reply.** In AWAITING_RESUME, records only queue. This is the state the plan's two-state client lacks.
199	- **No call ever blocks:** the reply is polled with `recv` from `pump`, and a reply that never comes ends at the 2 s deadline (the same 2 s `storage_feed` waits). After that the sender disconnects and retries with backoff.
200	- **Own counter:** `has_own` becomes 1 after the first successful send in this process and stays 1 across reconnects. That's what lets storage see a `kill -9` loss as a hole (PF-03).
201	- **Storage sends nothing after the reply.** Anything received in SENDING is `ipc_bad_message`: disconnect and reconnect.
202	- **Events are returned as flags** (`storage_unreachable`, `storage_reconnected`, `hub_queue_full`), and the hub logs them, as `gt_ipc_client` does.
203	- **Queue full (`hub_queue_full`):** refuse and count, as the client ring does. The GAP needs 2 free slots, and the order is old records, then the GAP, then new ones. - **The health tracker is generic** (`sensor_health`), not light-only, so the soil process can reuse it. It is a small public struct with no malloc.
- **Health input:** any non-`GT_OK` result from `gt_light_read` counts as one failure. The driver's 3 retries are already inside a single failed read.
- **Health output:** `gt_health_record` returns a transition event (`NONE` / `OFFLINE` / `ONLINE`) and the caller logs it. The tracker does no I/O.
- **Time is passed in** as `now_ms`, matching `gt_sampler_tick`, so tests need no clock.
- **Test ID prefixes:** `SHR` (sensor health record), `SHS` (sensor health should-read), `SHE` (sensor health event name), `LGF` (log format), `MSE` (message encode), `MSD` (message decode), `CRC` (CRC-32), `RCE` (record encode), `RCD` (record decode), `IFD` (IPC frame decode), `ICO` (IPC client open), `ICC` (IPC client close), `ICS` (IPC client send), `ICR` (IPC client reconnect), `IOV` (IPC client overflow), `IPL` (IPC loopback over a real socket).
- **Log ownership:** the light sensor's events (`i2c_read_error`, `sensor_offline`, `sensor_online`) are Lily's, as the light process's read-failure handling. The shared formatter (`gt_log_format`) has no owner in the Ownership map because every component uses it, so it counts as **Joint → Architecture integration**. Lily writes it first, as its first caller; give Lucas a heads-up so his components reuse it.
- **Log line:** `<timestamp_us> <LEVEL> <component> <event>[ key=value ...]`. The timestamp is µs since the Unix epoch, as a plain integer, the same unit as the on-disk record, so logs and records can be joined. The levels are `DEBUG` / `INFO` / `WARN` / `ERROR`. The light process logs `sensor_offline` as WARN and `sensor_online` as INFO.
- **Log sink: stderr** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-18). The formatter only fills a caller-provided buffer, and every process writes the finished `gt_log_format` line to stderr, as `storage_main` already does. Children inherit the supervisor's stderr, so under systemd every line lands in the journal. Each process still reads the wall clock for its own timestamps. A shared file sink was rejected (rotation becomes our problem), and so was sending lines to the monitor process (it waits on Mechanism E).
- **Hop 2 (hub→storage) carries the 24 B on-disk record** (decided 2026-10-23). The hub stamps `seq` and the µs timestamp, builds the record (CRC included), and storage checks it (amended 2026-10-26, PF-01: the timestamp is stamped on arrival, `seq` + CRC at send time; see *Hub contract (hop 2)*) with `gt_record_decode`, then appends it unchanged. There are two reasons. First, DESIGN.md already has the hub stamping the time and storage reading *records* from `storage.sock`. Second, a record that waits in the hub's 1024-record queue during a storage outage (up to about 17 min) keeps its real receive time. If storage stamped the time instead, the timestamp would be off by however long the record waited.
- **The hub's next `seq` after connecting to storage is max(own next, `seq_resume` + 1)** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-03). A freshly started hub has no counter, so it takes storage's reply + 1 (0 on an empty log). A running hub keeps its own counter, defined as 1 + the last `seq` whose `send()` succeeded, so records storage lost in a `kill -9` (unsynced, or still in the socket) leave a hole that storage turns into a GAP (`recovery_gap`). The alternative, always continuing from the reply, was rejected: it reuses the lost `seq`s, so the loss leaves no GAP and the hub's sent log holds duplicates, which breaks "no reading is lost silently" and the Evaluation plan's lost-readings formula. Only a loss where the hub restarts too (power cut) is shown by `unclean_shutdown` alone, which DESIGN.md's Power row already allows. Storage needed no change: its sequence guard already writes the GAP. This rule sets what PF-01 (when to stamp) and PF-02 (the sender's states) must support, and what `storage_faults.sh` checks (PF-04/05).
- **Hub contract for hop 2** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-01/PF-02): the hub stamps the time on arrival and `seq` + CRC at send; the socket seam gains `recv`; the sender waits for `seq_resume` (2 s deadline) before sending anything. See *Hub contract (hop 2)*.
- **Message magic is `0xA6`** (proposed), distinct from the on-disk record's `0xA7`, so a record can never be misread as a message.
- **Truncated messages are rejected at `recv()`,** which must return exactly `GT_MSG_SIZE`, not in decode. Decode keeps its fixed 16 B array.
- **Range checks stay in the hub:** decode doesn't check that light ≤ 65535. That is the hub's `reading_invalid` check.
- **Deferred:** `src/light_sensor_main.c` (open → sample → health → send) waited until the IPC client existed. The client was completed on 2026-10-24, so it is now the next item (see *Not done yet*).
- **`hub.sock` is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`** (decided 2026-10-24). The kernel keeps message boundaries, so each `send()` is one whole 16 B message and each `recv()` returns exactly one message. A short message shows up as a short `recv()`, which is where DESIGN.md rejects it, and there are no partial sends to track. `SOCK_STREAM` would need frame reassembly and resync code in the hub.
- **`hub_listen` stands in for the hub on the Pi** (decided 2026-10-24) until `gt_hub_accept` and the hub process exist. It's a small tool (`src/hub_listen_main.c`, `make hub_listen`) that prints each decoded message and flags counter gaps. With it, the kill -9 / kill -STOP fault tests can run now.
- **The client never blocks the sampler:** every socket call is non-blocking, and `send` uses `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, so a dead hub returns `EPIPE` instead of raising SIGPIPE, which would kill the sensor process.
- **Time is passed in** (`now_ms` on `gt_ipc_client_send` / `_pump`), as with the health tracker, so the backoff tests need no clock and no sleeps.
- **Events are returned, not logged:** the client returns `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` / `_RECONNECT` / `_OVERFLOW` bit flags, and the caller logs `ipc_disconnect` / `ipc_reconnect` / `ipc_overflow`, the same pattern as `gt_health_record`.
- **`gt_ipc_client_open` doesn't connect.** A hub that isn't up yet is not an error (DESIGN.md, Mechanism E: processes tolerate unavailable peers at startup). The first attempt happens on the first send or pump.
- **GAP needs 2 free slots:** after an overflow, a new reading is accepted only when the ring can hold both the GAP and the reading. This keeps the order: old data, then the GAP, then new data. Otherwise the reading is refused and counted into the same gap.
- **Close drops the buffer:** `gt_ipc_client_close` sends nothing more. Readings still in the ring are lost, and that's documented, not silent.
- **Limitation (no app-level ack):** a message the kernel accepted but the hub never `recv()`d before dying is lost. The hub sees the jump in the counter as a `sensor_seq_gap`.
- **`gt_ipc_client_open_ops` is declared in `ipc_sock.h`, not `ipc.h`** (Step 11). `ipc_sock.h` includes `ipc.h`, so putting it in `ipc.h` would make the two headers include each other. `gt_light_open_bus` sits next to its seam in `light_sensor.h` for the same reason.
- **Ownership of the ctx:** once `ops` is non-NULL, the client owns the ctx and calls `destroy` exactly once, from `close` or straight away if the client can't be allocated. With NULL ops there's no `destroy` to call, so the caller keeps the ctx.
- **`send` drains, pushes, then drains again** (Step 18). Draining before the push sends older frames first, which can free the slot the new reading needs, so a reading isn't refused when the hub could already have taken the backlog.
- **Any send result other than OK or FULL counts as the hub gone** (Step 19): disconnect, report `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` and retry after the wait. Both failure paths (a failed connect and a lost hub) share `schedule_retry`, so the wait doubles the same way for each.
- **Order moved to fit the link** (decided 2026-10-24). Every test binary links every file in `src/`, so nothing in `src/` may call a function that doesn't exist yet. `gt_ipc_client_open` calls `gt_ipc_sock_linux`, so it moved from Step 16 to Step 22, and its tests ICO-03/04 moved from Step 15 to Step 21. ICC-03 needs `send` to leave a frame in the ring, so it moved from Step 17 to Step 18.
- **One listener per socket, enforced by a lock** (decided 2026-10-24). A process that listens on a socket (`hub_listen` now; the hub and storage later) first takes an `fcntl` write lock on `<socket>.lock` and holds it for its whole life. Only the lock holder may remove a leftover socket file and bind a new one; a second copy prints `already running` and exits without touching anything. The kernel drops the lock when the holder dies, `kill -9` included, so a crash never leaves a stale lock. This is safer than probing with `connect()`, which leaves a gap: two copies started together could both see the file as stale, and the second would take the first one's address. Closing *any* fd the process holds on the lock file releases the lock, so the file is opened in one place only. When the hub is written, this moves into a shared `src/` helper; testing it needs `fork()`, because a process never blocks on its own `fcntl` lock.
- **Hub range check for soil rejects only `0xFFFF`** (decided 2026-10-27). That is the seesaw's error code; every other raw count is stored, so an open-air or very wet reading is kept and flagged rather than dropped. It sits behind `GT_HUB_SOIL_RAW_MAX` (`0xFFFE`), which Lucas can tighten once the soil driver exists. Light stays 0–65535. The nominal 200–2000 range was rejected: readings just outside it would be lost.
- **A sensor restart is logged, not turned into a GAP** (decided 2026-10-27). When a sensor's new connection starts with a counter below the one expected (the process restarted and its counter went back to 0), the hub logs `sensor_restart last_seen_us=… first_us=…` and writes no GAP record. The hub can't know how many readings the dead process lost, so any count would be made up; the two timestamps show the hole. A GAP with count 0 and one with a count estimated from the elapsed time were both rejected.
- **The hub is built before `light_sensor_main.c`** (decided 2026-10-27). The hub steps are H1–H9 and the light process is H10 (*Hub steps*), so the last step runs sensor → hub → storage end to end.
- **The socket seam is for clients; servers call the socket API directly** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-16). Clients (`gt_ipc_client`, and later the hub's hop-2 sender) go through `gt_sock_ops`, because their backoff, ring and resume logic is worth testing against a fake with no real waiting. Servers (`listen_sock.c`, `storage_server.c`, and later the hub's rx loop) call `socket` / `bind` / `listen` / `accept` / `recv` / `send` themselves and are tested over real sockets in a `/tmp` directory (LBD, SSV, and later the hub loopback). A server loop is mostly "wait in `poll()`, then hand the bytes on", which a real socket tests well. A server-side seam with its own fake was rejected: it would add an ops table and a second fake to test very little logic.

## Wire format: sensor → hub message (16 B, little-endian, encoded byte by byte)
| Off | Size | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | magic | `GT_MSG_MAGIC` = `0xA6` |
| 1 | 1 | version | `GT_MSG_VERSION` = 1 |
| 2 | 1 | type | `GT_MSG_DATA` = 1, `GT_MSG_GAP` = 2 (same values as `gt_rec_type`) |
| 3 | 1 | sensor_id | 1 light, 2 soil (0 = all is not valid on hop 1) |
| 4 | 4 | counter | sensor-side counter (for a GAP: the first refused counter) |
| 8 | 4 | seq | 0 from the sensor; the hub stamps it |
| 12 | 4 | value | DATA: raw count; GAP: refused-reading count |

Magic and version are written by encode and checked by decode. They are not `gt_msg` fields; `type` becomes one.

## Wire format: hub → storage record (24 B)
Hop 2 sends the on-disk record exactly as DESIGN.md *In what format → Record* lays it out: magic `0xA7`, type, version, sensor_id, seq (u32 at 4), timestamp (u64 µs at 8), value (u32 at 16) and CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 (at 20). `gt_record` and the codec live in `include/log_record.h`. **Watch the header order:** the record goes magic, **type, version**, sensor_id, while the message goes magic, **version, type**, sensor_id. Don't copy the message encoder without swapping those two bytes. Unlike the message, a GAP record may use sensor_id 0 (all).

## Hub contract (hop 2): stamping, numbering and the sender
Decided 2026-10-26 to settle PF-01 and PF-02 (Pipeline-Findings.md) before any hub code exists. It builds on the PF-03 numbering rule in *Decisions*. **Built 2026-10-28** in hub steps H1–H7, test first (see *Hub steps*).

**Why it changes (PF-01):** a hub that has just started doesn't know its next `seq` until storage's `seq_resume` reply arrives. Storage may be down or still recovering, and Mechanism E says the hub must keep running anyway. So the hub can't finish a record (`seq` + CRC) when the sensor message arrives. It finishes it when it sends it.

### Who stamps what, and when
| Field | Set by | When | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type`, `sensor_id`, `value` | `gt_hub_accept` | message arrives | copied from the checked message |
| `timestamp_us` | `gt_hub_accept` (`now_us` passed in) | message arrives | keeps the real receive time while the record waits in the queue (the 2026-10-23 reason still holds) |
| `seq` | the hop-2 sender | just before `send()` | only the sender knows the next `seq` (max rule) |
| CRC-32 | `gt_record_encode`, called by the sender | just before `send()` | the CRC covers `seq`, so it can't be computed earlier |

- **`gt_hub_accept`'s new contract:** validate, range-check and de-duplicate one `gt_msg`. On `GT_OK`, fill `*out` with type, sensor, value and `timestamp_us = now_us`, and leave `seq` at 0. The hub plan adds the event flags it returns (`reading_invalid`, `ipc_duplicate`, `sensor_seq_gap`). They're outside this contract.
- **The queue holds unstamped `gt_record`s:** 1024 slots of the in-memory struct (24 B with padding), so DESIGN.md's "1024 records × 24 B" budget still holds. A queued record has no `seq` and no CRC yet.
- **A `seq` is used only when `send()` returns `GT_OK`.** The sender stamps the queue head with `next_seq` and encodes it. On OK it drops the record and adds 1 to `next_seq`. On FULL or IO the record stays at the head, unchanged, and `next_seq` doesn't move, so a failed send never makes a hole in the numbering.

### The max rule, shared
- **`gt_next_seq`** (pure, in `include/storage_proto.h` next to `gt_resume`, because it says what the reply means): `gt_status gt_next_seq(int has_own, uint32_t own_next, const gt_resume *resume, uint32_t *next_out)`. It sets `*next_out` to max(`own_next`, `resume->seq` + 1). With `has_own` 0 (a fresh sender) it uses `resume->seq` + 1, or 0 when `resume->has_last` is 0. `GT_ERR_INVAL` for NULL arguments; `GT_ERR_FULL` when the reply's `seq` is `UINT32_MAX` (no next `seq` exists); `*next_out` is untouched on failure. Built and tested 2026-10-26 (NSQ 8/8).
- **Both callers use it:** the hop-2 sender and `storage_feed` (PF-04/05; `storage_feed` done 2026-10-26). The fault rounds then test the same numbering code the hub runs. `storage_proto.c` is Mechanism D's file, so give Lucas a heads-up.

### The socket seam gains `recv` (PF-02)
`gt_sock_ops` adds one op. The sensor client never calls it, but `src/ipc_sock.c` and `tests/fake_sock.h` both implement it:
```c
/* Receive one whole message into buf (cap bytes). Non-blocking.
 * GT_OK with *len_out = the message length, or *len_out = 0 when nothing
 * is waiting (EAGAIN); GT_ERR_IO when the peer closed (recv returns 0) or
 * reset the connection. */
gt_status (*recv)(void *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t cap, size_t *len_out);
```
- **The sender reads into `GT_RESUME_SIZE + 1` bytes**, like the storage and hub receivers, so an oversized reply shows up as too long.
- **`tests/fake_sock.h` grows:** scripted `recv` replies (bytes, "nothing yet", or IO), and its `sent` frames sized to 24 B as well as 16 B (they are fixed at `GT_MSG_SIZE` today).
- `gt_ipc_sock_linux(path)` already takes any path and sends any length, so it serves `storage.sock` unchanged apart from `recv`.

### Sender state machine (`include/hub_sender.h`, `src/hub_sender.c`)
```
              connect() OK → resume_deadline = now + 2000 ms
 DISCONNECTED ─────────────────────────────────────────────▶ AWAITING_RESUME
   ▲  attempt only when now ≥ next_attempt                        │ recv nothing yet → stay (until the deadline)
   │  backoff 100 ms → 2 s, as the client                         │ valid 8 B reply → gt_next_seq → SENDING
   │◀── deadline passes, or a bad / wrong-size reply ─────────────┤
   │    (ipc_bad_message), or recv IO: disconnect, retry later    │
   │                                                              ▼
   └──── send IO (EPIPE / ECONNRESET): head record kept ───── SENDING: drain oldest first,
         unstamped, storage_unreachable once                    stamp seq + encode + send;
                                                                FULL → stop, stay connected
```
- **Nothing is sent before the reply.** In AWAITING_RESUME, records only queue. This is the state the plan's two-state client lacks.
- **No call ever blocks:** the reply is polled with `recv` from `pump`, and a reply that never comes ends at the 2 s deadline (the same 2 s `storage_feed` waits). After that the sender disconnects and retries with backoff.
- **Own counter:** `has_own` becomes 1 after the first successful send in this process and stays 1 across reconnects. That's what lets storage see a `kill -9` loss as a hole (PF-03).
- **Storage sends nothing after the reply.** Anything received in SENDING is `ipc_bad_message`: disconnect and reconnect.
- **Events are returned as flags** (`storage_unreachable`, `storage_reconnected`, `hub_queue_full`), and the hub logs them, as `gt_ipc_client` does.
- **Queue full (`hub_queue_full`):** refuse and count, as the client ring does. The GAP needs 2 free slots, and the order is old records, then the GAP, then new ones. The GAP is `{type GAP, sensor_id 0, timestamp_us = the first refused reading's receive time, value = refused count}`, and it gets its `seq` at send like any other record.
- **API shape:** `gt_hub_sender_open_ops(ops, ctx)` (doesn't connect; owns the ctx as the client does), `gt_hub_sender_push(sender, const gt_record *unstamped, now_ms)` → OK / FULL / INVAL, `gt_hub_sender_pump(sender, now_ms)` → event flags, `gt_hub_sender_close`, and a stats getter (queued, refused, `next_seq`, `has_own`).

### Test prefixes (reserved; none collide with the existing ones)
`NSQ` next seq (fresh, running, empty log, reply ahead of the counter, NULL), `HAC` hub accept (fields, `seq` left 0, timestamp), `HSO` sender open/close, `HSR` resume wait (deadline, bad reply, IO, nothing sent before the reply), `HSS` sending (stamp on OK only, FULL keeps the head, IO keeps the head, the counter survives a reconnect), `HSQ` queue full and GAP, `HSL` loopback against `gt_storage_serve` over a real socket (a storage restart in the middle leaves a GAP for a running sender and none after a SIGTERM). Added 2026-10-27 with *Hub steps*: `HTO` hub timeouts, `HEV` hub event names, `HRX` hub rx loop over real sockets, `LLP` light process loop.

### Follow-ups this contract creates
- **DESIGN.md:** done 2026-10-26. The Hub → storage rows, the hub-queue budget and *At what rate* now say a record gets its `seq` + CRC when it is sent.
- **`include/hub.h`:** done 2026-10-28 (H2): `gt_hub_accept` leaves `seq` at 0.

## Health state machine
```
          10th consecutive failure → EV_OFFLINE, next_probe = now + 5000
 ONLINE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────▶ OFFLINE
   ▲  success → reset count                                     │ should_read() true only when now ≥ next_probe
   │  failure → count++ (no event before 10)                    │ failed probe → EV_NONE, next_probe = now + 5000
   └────────────────────── success → EV_ONLINE, count = 0 ◀─────┘

### Hub steps (H1–H10)
Planned 2026-10-27. These build *Hub contract (hop 2)* plus the hub's receive side, its process main and the light process. The workflow is the same as above: tests first, one function or one test case per write.

**Two clocks:** records are stamped with the wall clock (µs) and timeouts and backoff use the monotonic clock (ms). Both are passed in one struct, so no hub function takes more than 5 parameters:
```c
typedef struct { uint64_t wall_us; uint64_t mono_ms; } gt_hub_clock;
```

**`gt_hub_accept(hub, conn_id, message, now, result)`** (pure logic, `src/hub.c`):
- `conn_id` is a number the rx loop gives each accepted connection, counting up. It isn't the fd, because fds are reused after `close`.
- `result` holds the unstamped `gt_record`, `has_record`, the event flags, and the numbers the log lines need (`expected_counter`, `last_seen_us`).
- Value out of range → `GT_ERR_CORRUPT` + `reading_invalid`, and nothing is queued.
- Same connection, counter below the expected one → dropped (`ipc_duplicate`, no record).
- Counter above the expected one → queued, and `sensor_seq_gap` is logged.
- A new `conn_id` for a sensor → `NEW_CLIENT`, and the rx loop closes any older connection for it (`sensor_duplicate_client`). If the counter went back, it's also `sensor_restart` (log only, *Decisions*).
- A sensor's GAP message → a GAP record stamped with that sensor's last DATA receive time (the earliest the gap could have started, as in PF-07), or now if there is none. The next expected counter is `counter + value`.
- The first message from a stale sensor → `sensor_resumed`.

**`gt_hub_check_timeouts(hub, now_ms)`** returns a bitmask of the sensors that just went stale (3 s light, 180 s soil). The timers start when the hub is created, so a sensor that never connects is reported once.

**The rx loop `gt_hub_serve`** (a server, so it uses real sockets, PF-16):
- `poll()` waits on the listener, up to 8 sensor connections and `stop_fd`, with a 100 ms timeout.
- Each frame: `gt_ipc_frame_decode` → `gt_hub_accept` → `gt_hub_sender_push`.
- Every pass: check timeouts, then pump the sender.

**`hub_main HUB_SOCK STORAGE_SOCK`:**
- The lock and bind on `hub.sock`, and log lines to stderr.
- On SIGTERM it drains the queue for up to 1 s, then logs `hub_stop sent=N first_seq=A last_seq=B dropped=Q`, which is the range `log_verify --sent A..B` takes (PF-12).

135	## Wire format: sensor → hub message (16 B, little-endian, encoded byte by byte)
136	| Off | Size | Field | Value |
137	|---|---|---|---|
138	| 0 | 1 | magic | `GT_MSG_MAGIC` = `0xA6` |
139	| 1 | 1 | version | `GT_MSG_VERSION` = 1 |
140	| 2 | 1 | type | `GT_MSG_DATA` = 1, `GT_MSG_GAP` = 2 (same values as `gt_rec_type`) |
141	| 3 | 1 | sensor_id | 1 light, 2 soil (0 = all is not valid on hop 1) |
142	| 4 | 4 | counter | sensor-side counter (for a GAP: the first refused counter) |
143	| 8 | 4 | seq | 0 from the sensor; the hub stamps it |
144	| 12 | 4 | value | DATA: raw count; GAP: refused-reading count |
145	
146	Magic and version are written by encode and checked by decode. They are not `gt_msg` fields; `type` becomes one.
147	
148	## Wire format: hub → storage record (24 B)
149	Hop 2 sends the on-disk record exactly as DESIGN.md *In what format → Record* lays it out: magic `0xA7`, type, version, sensor_id, seq (u32 at 4), timestamp (u64 µs at 8), value (u32 at 16) and CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 (at 20). `gt_record` and the codec live in `include/log_record.h`. **Watch the header order:** the record goes magic, **type, version**, sensor_id, while the message goes magic, **version, type**, sensor_id. Don't copy the message encoder without swapping those two bytes. Unlike the message, a GAP record may use sensor_id 0 (all).

151	## Hub contract (hop 2): stamping, numbering and the sender
152	Decided 2026-10-26 to settle PF-01 and PF-02 (Pipeline-Findings.md) before any hub code exists. It builds on the PF-03 numbering rule in *Decisions*. **Built 2026-10-28** in hub steps H1–H7, test first (see *Hub steps*).
153	
154	**Why it changes (PF-01):** a hub that has just started doesn't know its next `seq` until storage's `seq_resume` reply arrives. Storage may be down or still recovering, and Mechanism E says the hub must keep running anyway. So the hub can't finish a record (`seq` + CRC) when the sensor message arrives. It finishes it when it sends it.
155	
156	### Who stamps what, and when
157	| Field | Set by | When | Why |
158	|---|---|---|---|
159	| `type`, `sensor_id`, `value` | `gt_hub_accept` | message arrives | copied from the checked message |
160	| `timestamp_us` | `gt_hub_accept` (`now_us` passed in) | message arrives | keeps the real receive time while the record waits in the queue (the 2026-10-23 reason still holds) |
161	| `seq` | the hop-2 sender | just before `send()` | only the sender knows the next `seq` (max rule) |
162	| CRC-32 | `gt_record_encode`, called by the sender | just before `send()` | the CRC covers `seq`, so it can't be computed earlier |
163	
164	- **`gt_hub_accept`'s new contract:** validate, range-check and de-duplicate one `gt_msg`. On `GT_OK`, fill `*out` with type, sensor, value and `timestamp_us = now_us`, and leave `seq` at 0. The hub plan adds the event flags it returns (`reading_invalid`, `ipc_duplicate`, `sensor_seq_gap`). They're outside this contract.
165	- **The queue holds unstamped `gt_record`s:** 1024 slots of the in-memory struct (24 B with padding), so DESIGN.md's "1024 records × 24 B" budget still holds. A queued record has no `seq` and no CRC yet.
166	- **A `seq` is used only when `send()` returns `GT_OK`.** The sender stamps the queue head with `next_seq` and encodes it. On OK it drops the record and adds 1 to `next_seq`. On FULL or IO the record stays at the head, unchanged, and `next_seq` doesn't move, so a failed send never makes a hole in the numbering.

168	### The max rule, shared
169	- **`gt_next_seq`** (pure, in `include/storage_proto.h` next to `gt_resume`, because it says what the reply means): `gt_status gt_next_seq(int has_own, uint32_t own_next, const gt_resume *resume, uint32_t *next_out)`. It sets `*next_out` to max(`own_next`, `resume->seq` + 1). With `has_own` 0 (a fresh sender) it uses `resume->seq` + 1, or 0 when `resume->has_last` is 0. `GT_ERR_INVAL` for NULL arguments; `GT_ERR_FULL` when the reply's `seq` is `UINT32_MAX` (no next `seq` exists); `*next_out` is untouched on failure. Built and tested 2026-10-26 (NSQ 8/8).
170	- **Both callers use it:** the hop-2 sender and `storage_feed` (PF-04/05; `storage_feed` done 2026-10-26). The fault rounds then test the same numbering code the hub runs. `storage_proto.c` is Mechanism D's file, so give Lucas a heads-up.

172	### The socket seam gains `recv` (PF-02)
173	`gt_sock_ops` adds one op. The sensor client never calls it, but `src/ipc_sock.c` and `tests/fake_sock.h` both implement it:
174	```c
175	/* Receive one whole message into buf (cap bytes). Non-blocking.
176	 * GT_OK with *len_out = the message length, or *len_out = 0 when nothing
177	 * is waiting (EAGAIN); GT_ERR_IO when the peer closed (recv returns 0) or
178	 * reset the connection. */
179	gt_status (*recv)(void *ctx, uint8_t *buf, size_t cap, size_t *len_out);
180	```
181	- **The sender reads into `GT_RESUME_SIZE + 1` bytes**, like the storage and hub receivers, so an oversized reply shows up as too long.
182	- **`tests/fake_sock.h` grows:** scripted `recv` replies (bytes, "nothing yet", or IO), and its `sent` frames sized to 24 B as well as 16 B (they are fixed at `GT_MSG_SIZE` today).
183	- `gt_ipc_sock_linux(path)` already takes any path and sends any length, so it serves `storage.sock` unchanged apart from `recv`.

185	### Sender state machine (`include/hub_sender.h`, `src/hub_sender.c`)
186	```
187	              connect() OK → resume_deadline = now + 2000 ms
188	 DISCONNECTED ─────────────────────────────────────────────▶ AWAITING_RESUME
189	   ▲  attempt only when now ≥ next_attempt                        │ recv nothing yet → stay (until the deadline)
190	   │  backoff 100 ms → 2 s, as the client                         │ valid 8 B reply → gt_next_seq → SENDING
191	   │◀── deadline passes, or a bad / wrong-size reply ─────────────┤
192	   │    (ipc_bad_message), or recv IO: disconnect, retry later    │
193	   │                                                              ▼
194	   └──── send IO (EPIPE / ECONNRESET): head record kept ───── SENDING: drain oldest first,
195	         unstamped, storage_unreachable once                    stamp seq + encode + send;
196	                                                                FULL → stop, stay connected
197	```
198	- **Nothing is sent before the reply.** In AWAITING_RESUME, records only queue. This is the state the plan's two-state client lacks.
199	- **No call ever blocks:** the reply is polled with `recv` from `pump`, and a reply that never comes ends at the 2 s deadline (the same 2 s `storage_feed` waits). After that the sender disconnects and retries with backoff.
200	- **Own counter:** `has_own` becomes 1 after the first successful send in this process and stays 1 across reconnects. That's what lets storage see a `kill -9` loss as a hole (PF-03).
201	- **Storage sends nothing after the reply.** Anything received in SENDING is `ipc_bad_message`: disconnect and reconnect.
202	- **Events are returned as flags** (`storage_unreachable`, `storage_reconnected`, `hub_queue_full`), and the hub logs them, as `gt_ipc_client` does.
203	- **Queue full (`hub_queue_full`):** refuse and count, as the client ring does. The GAP needs 2 free slots, and the order is old records, then the GAP, then new ones. The GAP is `{type GAP, sensor_id 0, timestamp_us = the first refused reading's receive time, value = refused count}`, and it gets its `seq` at send like any other record.
204	- **API shape:** `gt_hub_sender_open_ops(ops, ctx)` (doesn't connect; owns the ctx as the client does), `gt_hub_sender_push(sender, const gt_record *unstamped, now_ms)` → OK / FULL / INVAL, `gt_hub_sender_pump(sender, now_ms)` → event flags, `gt_hub_sender_close`, and a stats getter (queued, refused, `next_seq`, `has_own`).

222:## IPC client: connection and ring rules
223-```
224-                 connect() OK → wait = 100 ms
225-                 (EV_RECONNECT only if a disconnect or failed attempt came before)
226- DISCONNECTED ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────▶ CONNECTED
227-   ▲  attempt only when now ≥ next_attempt                              │ drain ring oldest first:
228-   │  connect() fails → next_attempt = now + wait,                      │   send OK   → drop frame, keep going
229-   │                     wait = min(wait × 2, 2000 ms)                  │   send FULL → stop (EAGAIN), stay connected
230-   └──── send IO (EPIPE / ECONNRESET) → EV_DISCONNECT once, frame kept, ◀┘
231-                                        next_attempt = now + wait
232-```
233-- **Starting state:** the client starts DISCONNECTED with `next_attempt = 0`, so the first send or pump tries to connect straight away. A clean first connect fires no event.
234-- **Backoff:** the waits run 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1600 → 2000 ms, then stay at 2000 ms, so attempts fall at 0, 100, 300, 700, 1500, 3100, 5100 ms… Any successful connect resets the wait to 100 ms.

questions.question: Where should the 1000 ms schedule live? include/sampler.h declares gt_sampler but nothing implements it.

options.label: In light_loop (Recommended)
options.description: light_loop keeps an anchored next_due_ms: a tick reads only when due, pumps every time, and skips missed slots with sample_overrun (DESIGN row). main sleeps until the due time it returns. sampler.h stays unused for now.

options.label: Implement sampler.c
options.description: Build gt_sampler first (its own tests), then have light_loop call gt_sampler_tick with an emit callback that does health + send. More files and more steps.

options.label: main only

# H9 wrap-up + H10: the light process (`light_loop.c` + `light_sensor_main.c`)

## Context
Milestone 3's last component. The hub is done through H9 (sensor → hub → storage works in WSL). H10 adds the real light process, so on the Pi a BH1750 reading can travel sensor → hub → storage (IPC ladder rungs 3–4 and 6). The loop logic goes in a testable `src/light_loop.c` (LLP tests against `fake_i2c` + `fake_sock`). `src/light_sensor_main.c` only wires the clocks, signals, startup open retry and stderr, the way `src/hub_main.c` does.

Decided with the user: the 1000 ms schedule lives in `light_loop` (anchored, with `sample_overrun`), and `sampler.h` stays unused. H10 also covers the open retry at startup (in main), `light_saturated` and `sensor_reinit` (needs a new driver function). The heartbeat to `sup.sock` stays deferred to Mechanism E, as in `hub_main.c`.

## Part A: finish H9
- **Commit: nothing to do.** `4e2e60a hub works end-to-end` already holds the `resume_seq` fix (`hub_sender.h/.c`, `hub_server.c`, HSS-01) and the doc updates (DESIGN.md, Pipeline-Findings.md, Sensor-Pipeline.md). The working tree is clean. Tell the user rather than making an empty commit.
- **Run all three in WSL and show the output:**
  `wsl -e bash -lc 'cd /mnt/c/Users/lheer/OneDrive/Desktop/cs370/CS370_TermProject/The-Green-Thumb && make test && make asan && make memcheck'`
  If anything fails, stop and report. Don't touch tests.

## Part B: H10, in small steps (tests first, one function or test per turn)

### H10a: `sensor_reinit` driver tests (red): new `tests/test_light_reinit.c`, prefix `LSI`
- LSI-01 reinit sends POWER_ON, RESET, CONT_HRES, then waits 180 ms
- LSI-02 a NACKed init write gives GT_ERR_IO, bus kept open (the sensor is still usable and closes once)
- LSI-03 NULL sensor gives GT_ERR_INVAL
- Header comment, `/* ---- LSI-0N: ---- */` heads, `test_case_t` table, `RUN_TESTS`.

### H10b: `gt_light_reinit` (green): `include/light_sensor.h`, `src/light_sensor.c`
- Pull the three `send_cmd` calls + the 180 ms wait out of `gt_light_open_bus` into one `static gt_status init_chip(gt_light_sensor *s)`. `open_bus` keeps its close-and-free-on-failure behavior; `gt_light_reinit(s)` calls `init_chip` and returns its status without closing. The LSO tests must stay green unchanged.

### H10c: `include/light_loop.h` (API only; check with `-fsyntax-only`)
```c
#define GT_LIGHT_PERIOD_MS 1000
typedef void (*gt_light_log_fn)(void *log_ctx, gt_log_level level,
                                const char *event, const char *fields);   /* same shape as gt_hub_log_fn */
typedef struct { gt_light_sensor *sensor; gt_ipc_client *client;
                 gt_light_log_fn log; void *log_ctx; } gt_light_loop_ctx;   /* used, not owned */
typedef struct { gt_light_loop_ctx ctx; gt_health health;
                 uint32_t counter; uint64_t next_due_ms; } gt_light_loop;  /* public, no malloc, like gt_health */
gt_status gt_light_loop_init(gt_light_loop *loop, const gt_light_loop_ctx *ctx, uint64_t now_ms); /* first read due at now */
gt_status gt_light_loop_tick(gt_light_loop *loop, uint64_t now_ms, uint64_t *next_due_out);
```
**One tick, in order:**
1. If due and `gt_health_should_read`: read.
   - **Online:** the result goes to `gt_health_record`.
   - **Offline probe:** a good read runs `gt_light_reinit` (`sensor_reinit`), then reads again for a fresh value, and that read's result is what gets recorded.
2. Log the health event: `sensor_offline` WARN / `sensor_online` INFO, plus `i2c_read_error` WARN on every failed read.
3. A good value becomes a DATA `gt_msg {LIGHT, counter, value}`, sent with `gt_ipc_client_send`.
   - The counter advances on OK *and* FULL, so the client's GAP lines up with the hub's expected counter. It does not advance on a failed read (no message, so no false `sensor_seq_gap`).
   - A value of 0xFFFF is still sent, and logs `light_saturated` INFO.
4. If nothing was sent this tick, `gt_ipc_client_pump`. Log IPC events: `ipc_disconnect` WARN, `ipc_reconnect` INFO, `ipc_overflow` WARN `refused=N`.
5. Advance `next_due_ms` by one period. If `now` has already passed it, skip the missed slots (no burst), keep the anchor, and log `sample_overrun skipped=N` WARN.

### H10d: LLP tests (red): new `tests/test_light_loop.c`, written one case per turn
LLP-01 due tick reads and sends DATA counter 0 · LLP-02 counter goes up one per reading · LLP-03 a tick before it's due doesn't read but still pumps · LLP-04 failed read: i2c_read_error, nothing sent · LLP-05 10th failure logs sensor_offline once · LLP-06 a good probe reinits, then marks online · LLP-07 a failed reinit stays offline · LLP-08 0xFFFF is sent and logs light_saturated · LLP-09 overrun skips slots and keeps the anchor · LLP-10 hub down: one disconnect, one reconnect · LLP-11 a full ring logs ipc_overflow refused=N · LLP-12 NULL args give GT_ERR_INVAL.
- Logs go into a small in-file log book, the way `tests/test_hub_serve.c` does it.
- **Test-infra change, to approve:** LLP-11 needs 65+ readings, but `FAKE_I2C_MAX_READ` is 64 B (32 readings). Raise it to 256. There's precedent: `fake_sock` went 256 → 1100 in H6. No existing test depends on the cap.

### H10e: `src/light_loop.c` (green), one function per turn
Order: `init` → read/health/log helpers → send + IPC event logging → schedule/overrun. Each new `static` is used by the write that adds it (`-Werror`). Loops get an invariant comment.

### H10f: `src/light_sensor_main.c` + Makefile
- **Usage:** `light_sensor /dev/i2c-1 /run/plantpi/hub.sock`.
- **Copied from `hub_main.c`:** `wall_us` / `mono_ms`, a stderr `log_line` (component `light`), and SIGTERM/SIGINT handling (`volatile sig_atomic_t` stop flag; SIGPIPE ignored).
- **Startup open retry:** `gt_light_open` fails → `i2c_open_error` WARN each attempt and `sensor_offline` WARN once, retry every 5 s (`nanosleep`, so EINTR stops it early). Never exits on a missing sensor.
- **Run:**
  - `gt_ipc_client_open`, then `light_start`, then the loop `tick` → `clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, TIMER_ABSTIME, next_due)` until stop.
  - On stop, log `light_stop counter= sent= queued= refused=`. Queued frames are dropped, as already documented in "Close drops the buffer".
- **Makefile:** a `light_sensor` target modeled on `hub_main`, added to `all` and `.PHONY`.

### H10g: docs
Sensor-Pipeline.md:
- *Changes from the plan* bullets: the schedule in `light_loop`, `sampler.h` unused, `gt_light_reinit`, the counter rule, the fake_i2c cap.
- The *Not done yet* `light_sensor_main.c` bullet.
- The test prefixes line gets `LSI`.

Status table/Log only at end of day, when asked.

## Verification
- Each step: build and run only the affected binaries (`test_light_*`, `test_light_loop`). The user runs asan/memcheck between steps.
- End of H10: `make test && make asan && make memcheck` all green. `make light_sensor` builds with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
- WSL smoke: `build/light_sensor /dev/i2c-1 /tmp/x/hub.sock` with no I2C logs `i2c_open_error` every 5 s plus one `sensor_offline`, and SIGTERM exits cleanly.
- Pi (user): `storage_main` + `hub_main` + `light_sensor` for 10 min. Records reach storage, there are no counter gaps, covering the sensor drops the raw count, and `log_verify` passes. This is ladder rungs 3 and 6.

H10 also covers the open retry at startup (in main), `light_saturated` and `sensor_reinit` (needs a new driver function). The heartbeat to `sup.sock` stays deferred to Mechanism E, as in `hub_main.c`.

## Part A: finish H9

### H10a: `sensor_reinit` driver tests (red): new `tests/test_light_reinit.c`, prefix `LSI`
- LSI-01 reinit sends POWER_ON, RESET, CONT_HRES, then waits 180 ms
- LSI-02 a NACKed init write gives GT_ERR_IO, bus kept open (the sensor is still usable and closes once)
- LSI-03 NULL sensor gives GT_ERR_INVAL
- Header comment, `/* ---- LSI-0N: ---- */` heads, `test_case_t` table, `RUN_TESTS`.

### H10b: `gt_light_reinit` (green): `include/light_sensor.h`, `src/light_sensor.c`
- Pull the three `send_cmd` calls + the 180 ms wait out of `gt_light_open_bus` into one `static gt_status init_chip(gt_light_sensor *s)`. `open_bus` keeps its close-and-free-on-failure behavior; `gt_light_reinit(s)` calls `init_chip` and returns its status without closing. The LSO tests must stay green unchanged.

### H10c: `include/light_loop.h` (API only; check with `-fsyntax-only`)
```c
#define GT_LIGHT_PERIOD_MS 1000
typedef void (*gt_light_log_fn)(void *log_ctx, gt_log_level level,
                                const char *event, const char *fields);   /* same shape as gt_hub_log_fn */
typedef struct { gt_light_sensor *sensor; gt_ipc_client *client;
                 gt_light_log_fn log; void *log_ctx; } gt_light_loop_ctx;   /* used, not owned */
typedef struct { gt_light_loop_ctx ctx; gt_health health;
                 uint32_t counter; uint64_t next_due_ms; } gt_light_loop;  /* public, no malloc, like gt_health */
gt_status gt_light_loop_init(gt_light_loop *loop, const gt_light_loop_ctx *ctx, uint64_t now_ms); /* first read due at now */

```
**One tick, in order:**
1. If due and `gt_health_should_read`: read.

content.text:
H10a is done and red as expected. I wrote [tests/test_light_reinit.c](tests/test_light_reinit.c) with three cases:

- **LSI-01:** reinit re-sends POWER_ON, RESET and CONT_HRES, then waits a fresh 180 ms conversion. The bus stays open.
- **LSI-02:** for each of the three commands, a NACK makes reinit return `GT_ERR_IO`. It sends nothing after the failed command, doesn't wait and keeps the bus open, so the only close is the caller's `gt_light_close`.
- **LSI-03:** a NULL sensor returns `GT_ERR_INVAL`.

**Red check:** the build fails only on the missing function:
```
tests/test_light_reinit.c:38:14: error: implicit declaration of function 'gt_light_reinit'
```
Note that `make test` will fail at this binary until H10b lands, as in earlier red steps.

**qlty:**
- `light_sensor.c` and `light_sensor.h` currently have no smells.
- qlty never looks at the test files: `qlty smells tests/test_light_reinit.c` checked 0 files, because `.qlty/qlty.toml` excludes `**/test_*.*` from smells. The qlty gate therefore only covers `src/` and `include/`. I'll still keep the tests free of copy-paste.
- qlty is at `~/.qlty/bin/qlty` in WSL but isn't on the non-interactive PATH, so I call it by that full path.

**Next is H10b:** add `gt_light_reinit` to `light_sensor.h`, and move the init sequence in `light_sensor.c` into a `static init_chip` that `open_bus` and `reinit` share. Then LSI turns green, and LSO must stay green unchanged.

content.text:
H10c is done: [include/light_loop.h](include/light_loop.h) declares the light loop's API and documents it.

**What's in it:**
- **Top comment:** the five tick steps from the plan:
  1. Read, with the offline probe re-running the chip's init and then reading again.
  2. Health logging.
  3. Send, with `light_saturated` for 0xFFFF.
  4. Pump plus the IPC event lines.
  5. The anchored schedule with `sample_overrun`.

  It also states the counter rule. The counter goes up for every reading handed to the client, whether sent or refused, so the client's GAP covers the counters the hub expects. A failed read uses no counter, so the hub logs no false `sensor_seq_gap`.
- **`GT_LIGHT_PERIOD_MS`:** 1000.
- **`gt_light_log_fn`:** the log callback, the same shape as `gt_hub_log_fn`, with the function-pointer type explained in its comment.
- **`gt_light_loop_ctx`:** the sensor, client and log callback. The loop uses them but doesn't own them.
- **`gt_light_loop`:** a public struct with no malloc, like `gt_health`. It holds the ctx, the health tracker, `counter` and `next_due_ms`.
- **`gt_light_loop_init`:** returns `GT_ERR_INVAL` for any NULL among the loop, ctx, sensor, client or log, and leaves `*loop` untouched.
- **`gt_light_loop_tick`:** returns `GT_OK`, or `GT_ERR_INVAL` for a NULL loop. It sets `*next_due_out`, and NULL means ignore it.

**Checks:**
- **gcc:** `-fsyntax-only` with the project flags passes (`SYNTAX_OK`).
- **qlty:** `qlty smells` and `qlty check` both report no issues.
- **Tests:** none ran, because nothing includes the header yet.

**The helpers the later cases will reuse:**
- **Log book:** `record_log` captures each line's level, event and fields, so later cases can check `refused=N` and `skipped=N`.
- **`light_rig`:** holds the fake bus, the fake hub, the log book and the loop. It's `static` because `fake_sock` is about 35 KB, the same choice `test_hub_serve.c` made.
- **`start_rig(now)` and `stop_rig()`:** `start_rig` opens the sensor and client on fresh fakes and runs `gt_light_loop_init`; `stop_rig` closes both.
- **`push_reading(raw)` and `sent_message(i)`:** `push_reading` scripts a big-endian reading, and `sent_message` decodes the i-th message the hub received.

I only added helpers that LLP-01 uses, because an unused `static` would fail the build under `-Werror`. The `logged(event)` counter comes with the first case that needs it.

**LLP-01:** the first tick is due at start. It reads 300 and sends one DATA message: light sensor, counter 0, value 300, seq 0. It returns `next_due = 1000`, and a clean first connect logs nothing.

**Progress (2026-10-26):** PF-01 to PF-03 are settled on paper in both documents. Each finding below has a **Resolution** line saying what was decided and what is still to do. ## High: the `seq_resume` hand-off and the hub

These three come from the same change: on every connect, storage now sends the hub an 8 B `seq_resume` reply, and DESIGN.md says "the hub continues from the next value". They decide the hub's design, so they should be settled in the PR before the hub is written.

### PF-01: The hub can't stamp `seq` when a message arrives [Both docs] [Breaks plan]
## Contradicts DESIGN.md (storage)

### PF-06: Records from the end of a day go into the next day's segment
- **DESIGN.md:** "one segment file per UTC day".
- `gt_flusher_tick` rolls over to the new day's segment *before* it flushes ([src/storage_server.c:212-228](src/storage_server.c#L212-L228)), and `gt_storage_rollover` doesn't flush first. Up to about 60 s of records received before midnight are written into the new day's file.
- **Fix:** flush (or attempt to) before switching segments.
- **Resolution (2026-10-26):** the fix was adopted.
  - **The change:** `gt_storage_rollover` flushes pending records into the old segment before creating the new one, and its events are passed on. If that flush fails, the existing degraded path cuts the old tail and the records go into the new segment.
  - **Remaining limit:** records that arrive between midnight and the flusher's next pass (≤ 1 s) still go into the old day's file. This is now written in DESIGN.md.
  - **Tests:** SRO-13 and SRO-14 are new. SRO-11, SRO-12 and FTK-05 were changed with approval, because they asserted the old behaviour; each kept its scenario. All were seen red, then green.

### PF-07: A storage-made GAP record carries the gap's end time
- **DESIGN.md** record table: a GAP's timestamp is the "gap start"; "a gap ends at the timestamp of the next DATA record".
- `gt_seq_gap_record` uses the incoming record's timestamp ([src/storage_seq.c:42](src/storage_seq.c#L42)), so start and end come out identical and the gap's length is lost. Its `seq` (the first refused reading) and `value` are correct.
- **Resolution (2026-10-26):**
  - **The rule:** a storage-made GAP is stamped with the last accepted record's time, the earliest the gap could have started.

After a `kill -9`, the accepted-but-unsynced records are gone, so the reply is the last `seq` on disk. A hub that continues from there reuses the lost records' `seq`s: no hole appears, no GAP is written, and the hub's sent list holds the same `seq` twice, so the Evaluation plan's formula no longer works.

146:  - **Logging:** `gt_storage_log_commit` logs `storage_commit records=N commit_us=T fsync_us=F` at INFO, then `fsync_slow fsync_us=F records=N` at WARN for an fsync over 1 s. The flush thread calls it once per pass, and `storage_main` around the final shutdown.

N comes from the monotonic clock. A clock that is synced from the start logs neither. `retention_skipped` is unchanged.

It logs `clock_wait max_s=120`, then `clock_wait_done waited_s=N synced=0|1`. The hub's 1024-record queue covers the wait. "Empty log" comes from the new `gt_storage_log_empty` / `_ops`, which uses the same listing open uses (SOP-16, red then green).

The stop signals are blocked in the flush thread, SIGPIPE is ignored, and the exit status is honest. Seen working in the PF-04 run.

## Decisions (Mechanism D)
- **One pending buffer** (2026-10-26). The 64-record batch and the 1 MB outage queue are the same buffer: records stay in it until a flush succeeds. A flush writes everything pending.
- **Raw bytes are stored.** The pending buffer keeps the 24 B exactly as received and checked by `gt_record_decode`; a flush writes them unchanged, with no second encode.
- **Each pending record keeps its add time**, so a record that arrives during a slow flush is still flushed within the 62 s commit-latency target (about 350 KB at full capacity). The first version restarted the clock at commit; it was changed to stay inside the Evaluation plan.
- **The mutex lives inside `gt_storage`** and is never held during file I/O. `handle`, `committed_offset` and `degraded` belong to the one flushing thread.
- **Segment names use integer date maths, not `gmtime_r`:** on 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS `time_t` is 32 bits and `gmtime_r` fails after January 2038. Checked against Python for every day 1970–2100.
- **Recovery repairs only the newest segment**; if it holds no records, older segments are read for the last `seq`.
- **A clock behind the log keeps appending** to the newest segment instead of creating an earlier-dated one.
- **The shutdown is its own function** (`gt_storage_shutdown`), separate from `close`, so a failed final flush is reported and never followed by a marker. `close` writes nothing.
- **`unclean_shutdown` only when segments exist:** a fresh install is not a crash.
- **Backlog and full-buffer events:** `storage_backlog` once per threshold crossing (50/75/90%), `storage_degraded reason=queue_full` once per full spell. The GAP for refused readings comes for free from the sequence guard: refusing leaves the last accepted `seq` alone, so the next reading skips the refused ones.
- **Retention deletes only outside the window and beyond the newest 30**, so a clock that jumps forward can't wipe the history. Rollover while degraded first cuts the old segment's torn tail (Step 11b).

I've noted the reboot issue for after H10, and LLP-03 is added and red as expected. The file compiles cleanly under `-Werror` and fails only on the undefined `gt_light_loop_*` functions.

**The reboot issue:** I couldn't find the earlier session's discussion in the repo, so this is my best reading of the code. PF-06 in Pipeline-Findings.md only fixed the case where storage keeps running through midnight; it flushes the old day before rolling over. The reboot case is still open, and I see two possible causes. I'll check which one you mean when we start on it:
1. **Restart after midnight:** when storage starts, it reuses the newest segment only if that segment is dated today or later; otherwise it starts today's file ([src/storage_open.c:261-265](src/storage_open.c#L261-L265)). Records stamped before midnight that reach storage after it restarts are written into the new day's file. That covers records waiting in the hub queue and records arriving during the 120 s clock wait.
2. **Clock behind after a reboot:** the Pi has no hardware clock, so after a reboot its time may be behind. Today's records then go into yesterday's file until the clock syncs and rollover runs.

Either way, a likely fix is to pick the file from each record's own timestamp, which PF-06 rejected at the time as a bigger change. I saved this as a pending-work memory, so it will come up again after H10.

**LLP-03, "a tick before it's due doesn't read but pumps":**
- The hub refuses the first connect, so the reading taken at 0 ms waits in the client's ring.
- A tick at 500 ms makes no new bus read, which shows the loop didn't read early.
- The pump still runs: the 100 ms retry is due, so the client connects and the waiting message (value 300) reaches the hub.
- `next_due` stays anchored at 1000.

**Next is LLP-04:** a failed read logs `i2c_read_error`, sends nothing, and leaves the counter where it was. It brings in the `logged(event)` helper.

LLP-12 is added, so the LLP test file is complete with all 12 cases and red as expected. It compiles cleanly under `-Werror`, and the only link errors are the two functions not written yet, `gt_light_loop_init` and `gt_light_loop_tick`.

**New helper:** `check_init_rejects(ctx)` fills a loop with a known byte pattern, calls init with `ctx`, and checks that init returns `GT_ERR_INVAL` and left every byte unchanged. It compares with `memcmp` rather than `==`, because C can't compare two structs with `==`, and copying a struct with `=` doesn't have to copy its padding bytes. That second point is the same lesson IPL-05 ran into.

**LLP-12, "NULL args give GT_ERR_INVAL":**
- `init` rejects a NULL loop or a NULL ctx. It also rejects a ctx with a NULL sensor, a NULL client or a NULL log callback, and leaves the loop untouched in every case.
- `tick` rejects a NULL loop, and `*next_due_out` keeps its marker value.

**Next is H10e:** writing `src/light_loop.c`, one function per turn, in this order:
1. `gt_light_loop_init`.
2. The read and health part of `tick`, including the offline probe with reinit.
3. Sending, `light_saturated`, and logging the IPC events.
4. The anchored schedule and `sample_overrun`.

After each turn I'll run `test_light_loop` (some cases stay red until the later parts land) plus `qlty smells` and `qlty check` on `src/light_loop.c`.

**What I added to [src/light_loop.c](src/light_loop.c):**

- **`probe_offline`:** reads; if the read is good, re-runs the chip init. If the init succeeds, it logs `sensor_reinit` and reads again, returning that second read's result. A failed read or a refused init counts as a failed probe. It has one `return`, so it stays under qlty's return-count limit.
- **`log_health_event`:** logs `sensor_offline` at WARN or `sensor_online` at INFO, and nothing when there was no transition.

**What changed in [src/light_loop.c](src/light_loop.c):**
- **`ipc_event_lines`:** a small table that maps each client event flag to its log line: `ipc_disconnect` at WARN, `ipc_reconnect` at INFO, `ipc_overflow` at WARN. The plan called for a table rather than a chain of ifs, to keep qlty quiet.
- **`send_reading`:**
  - It logs `light_saturated` for a 0xFFFF reading, then sends one DATA message carrying the current counter.
  - The counter moves on when the client took the reading and when it refused it because the ring was full. It doesn't move on a NULL or bad message.

- **`overflow_fields`:** builds the `refused=N` text from `gt_ipc_client_stats`.
- **`log_ipc_events`:** one loop over the table, logging a line for each event flag that is set.
- **`tick`:** sends when there's a value; otherwise it pumps the client so the queue still drains. Then it logs any IPC events. The temporary `(void)have_value` is gone.

content.text:
I added the `tick_until` helper, and LLP now passes 12/12. That completes H10e: `src/light_loop.c` is fully written.

```
[LLP-01] a due tick reads and sends DATA counter 0     PASS
...
[LLP-12] NULL args give GT_ERR_INVAL                   PASS
12/12 tests passed
```
The command reported exit 1 only because I left a stray `grep -c … /dev/null` at the end of it. The test binary itself passed.

**What changed in [tests/test_light_loop.c](tests/test_light_loop.c):**
- **New helper:** `tick_until(probe_at_ms)` ticks once a second from just after the last failure up to the probe, the way the main would while the sensor is offline.
- **LLP-06 and LLP-07** call it right after `go_offline()`, so their probe tick is on time rather than a 5 s jump. Every check in both is unchanged, including LLP-06's ordering check, which now passes.
- **LLP-05** uses the same helper in place of its own loop. Its "no reads while offline" check is unchanged.

**The last code change, `advance_schedule`, in [src/light_loop.c](src/light_loop.c):**
- After a due tick, it moves the due time on by one period.
- If the tick ran late, it skips the missed slots, keeps the grid anchored and logs `sample_overrun skipped=N`.
- Due ticks keep the schedule moving even while the sensor is offline; `gt_health_should_read` still decides whether a tick actually reads.

**qlty:** `qlty smells` and `qlty check` on `src/light_loop.c` and `include/light_loop.h` both report no issues. Neither file changed after that run; the helper fix only touched the test file.

**Your full-suite run:** all binaries now link `src/light_loop.c`, and the `fake_i2c.h` read cap is now 256. `test_light_loop`, `test_light_reinit` and the other light tests pass in the targeted runs. `make test`, `make asan` and `make memcheck` are yours to run.

**Next is H10f:** `src/light_sensor_main.c` and its Makefile target. That covers the clocks, the signals, the startup open retry and the stderr log lines, then a WSL smoke run with no I2C to check the `i2c_open_error` retry and that SIGTERM exits cleanly.

HEADERS := $(wildcard include/*.h tests/*.h)

# Every tests/test_*.c becomes $(BUILD)/test_* linked against all of LIB_SRC.
TEST_SRC := $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)

	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

storage_main: $(BUILD)/storage_main

	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

TEST_BINS := $(patsubst tests/%.c,$(BUILD)/%,$(TEST_SRC))

VALGRIND := valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all --error-exitcode=1

all: $(TEST_BINS) $(BUILD)/light_probe $(BUILD)/light_sensor $(BUILD)/hub_listen $(BUILD)/hub_main $(BUILD)/storage_main $(BUILD)/storage_feed $(BUILD)/log_verify

$(BUILD)/%: tests/%.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

# On-Pi BH1750 bring-up check (see src/light_probe_main.c). Not run by
# `make test`: it needs real I2C hardware.
$(BUILD)/light_probe: src/light_probe_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

light_probe: $(BUILD)/light_probe

# The light sensor process (see src/light_sensor_main.c): BH1750 readings
# to hub.sock. Not run by `make test`: it runs until SIGTERM, and reads
# real I2C (without it, it logs i2c_open_error and retries every 5 s).
$(BUILD)/light_sensor: src/light_sensor_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

light_sensor: $(BUILD)/light_sensor

# On-Pi stand-in for the hub on hub.sock (see src/hub_listen_main.c). Not
# run by `make test`: it serves until killed.
$(BUILD)/hub_listen: src/hub_listen_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

hub_listen: $(BUILD)/hub_listen

# The hub process (see src/hub_main.c): sensors on hub.sock, records to
# storage.sock. Not run by `make test`: it serves until SIGTERM.
$(BUILD)/hub_main: src/hub_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

hub_main: $(BUILD)/hub_main

# The storage process (see src/storage_main.c). Not run by `make test`: it
# serves until SIGTERM.
$(BUILD)/storage_main: src/storage_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

storage_main: $(BUILD)/storage_main

# Load generator standing in for the hub on storage.sock (see
# src/storage_feed_main.c). Not run by `make test`: it needs storage_main.
$(BUILD)/storage_feed: src/storage_feed_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

storage_feed: $(BUILD)/storage_feed

# Offline log verifier (see src/log_verify_main.c), used after every fault
# test. Not run by `make test`: it needs a real log directory.
$(BUILD)/log_verify: src/log_verify_main.c $(LIB_SRC) $(HEADERS)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LIB_SRC) $< -o $@

log_verify: $(BUILD)/log_verify

# Every test binary runs even if an earlier one fails; failures are listed
# at the end and the target still exits nonzero for CI.
test: $(TEST_BINS)
	@failed=""; for b in $(TEST_BINS); do echo "== $$b"; ./$$b || failed="$$failed $$b"; done; \
	if [ -n "$$failed" ]; then echo "FAILED:$$failed"; exit 1; fi

# Sanitizers get their own build dirs so they never reuse plain objects.
asan:
	$(MAKE) test BUILD=build/asan \
	  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

ubsan:
	$(MAKE) test BUILD=build/ubsan \
	  EXTRA_CFLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=undefined"

# valgrind and ASan don't mix, so memcheck runs the plain build.
memcheck: $(TEST_BINS)
	@failed=""; for b in $(TEST_BINS); do echo "== valgrind $$b"; $(VALGRIND) ./$$b || failed="$$failed $$b"; done; \
	if [ -n "$$failed" ]; then echo "FAILED:$$failed"; exit 1; fi

clean:
	rm -rf build
